note: The passenger ship's lane and the hidden deadline. All x,z in world metres on the sea plane (the lighthouse is at 5, -8.5; the island fills about -45..45 on both axes; the player's boat runs south from the dock at -27, 18 to the Saltgate at 6, 531). Retune here, then run tools/test_ship_route.gd.

deadline.length_note: The Easy length and the fallback (creator, 2 Nov 2026, T19; was 3 min 30 s from 26 Oct, Decisions A28). After the play check (T60) the creator chose difficulty levels instead of one length: see difficulty_length_s.
deadline.difficulty_note: Chosen on the title screen (GameSettings.difficulty; creator, 2 Nov 2026, T60): Easy 3:00, Medium 2:30, Hard 2:00. length_s is the fallback when no difficulty applies.

ship.saved_speed_note: Once the beacon is lit the ship makes for port at this multiple of its approach speed, so the win card does not wait minutes (the turn rate is unchanged, so the turn is wider; tools/test_ship_route.gd checks the clearance).

approach.note: The lane the ship holds with no beacon: in from the north-east (the creator, 29 Oct 2026: out along the coast to the right of the return crossing, so the lamp room and the boat both see it), then a straight run west-south-west onto the grounding rock. It is the ship's CENTRE line. The last point is where the centre sits when the bow touches the rock. The deadline expires commit_distance_m before it; from then on the ship can no longer turn and runs on to the rock.

safe_lane.note: Where the ship goes once the burner is fitted: it keeps to the approach lane as far as its first point (first_is_approach_index, skipped if it is already past it), then steers (turn_rate_deg_s) through these points, past the rock on its east side and on towards Saint Calder.

grounding_rock.note: The nearest sea stack to the island (about 80 m off its south shore). It also sits beside the player's return route, so a crash is visible from the boat.

crash.note: Placeholder grounding: the ship rides up on the rock, lists, sinks slowly and its lights die. A real break-up needs art (T08).

lights.note: T44 (1 Nov 2026): the ship is lit the way a liner is at night, with nothing floating off the hull. Lit windows are small emissive panes laid flat on the model's own hull and superstructure (found by casting rays at the mesh), the navigation lights and deck lanterns sit on the real lantern posts and mast tops, and two small warm lights spill onto the hull and the water only when the camera is close. Everything is emissive and fog-proof so the ship reads at the horizon. Local ship frame: bow is -Z, starboard +X, keel at y 0 (the waterline is about y 2.4).

windows.rows_note: Rows of lit windows: portholes in the black hull (8.3 and 9.8, where the texture has its porthole dots), the promenade deck (14.2) and the upper tier (17.2) on both sides, and the superstructure's forward face and bridge (18.0, 20.3) and after face (16.6, 19.5), so a ship seen bow-on still shows lit windows. Each window sits where a ray from outside meets an upright wall (rail tops and decks are looked past); it is dropped where the wall is set back past min_out_m (metres out from the centreline, or from midships for an end row), where it juts out from its neighbours by more than max_jump_m (lifeboats, posts), or where lit_fraction says that cabin is dark.
windows.grow_note: Far away each pane grows in its own plane (wider more than taller) so at 700 m the windows run together into lit decks instead of vanishing; they stay flat on the hull, never balls of light.

lights.lamps_note: Mounted on the model: the white masthead lights on the fore (28.4 m) and aft (30.9 m) mast tops, the red and green sidelights in the bridge-wing lanterns, the white stern light on the stern rail, and the two ornamental globe lanterns fore and aft lit as deck lamps. Each shows only in its sector as on a real ship (masthead 225 deg ahead, sidelights 112.5 deg each side, stern 135 deg astern), so the lights also tell the player which way she is heading.
lights.halo_note: Each lamp has a soft glow (rain haze) that grows with distance (distance x halo_per_m, from halo_m up to halo_max_m) so it keeps a few pixels at the horizon.

spill.note: Two warm OmniLights just off the hull, for the light the windows throw on the hull plating and the water. They are only switched on while the camera is within live_within_m (the launch near the crash), when the interior lights are off, so they stay inside the Lighting budget (max_dynamic_lights 18).
